description:
Root: one published transport boundary fragments into multiple native callable boundaries because its resolution set is over-specialized. Distinct from the capture-layout invariant (f98.3) and from f98.7 (which publishes ZERO boundaries -- see below); this is purely the callable-boundary system.

Reproduced on HEAD (`Enum.to_list(1..7//2)`):
  error[artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan]: native callable materialization for FunctionId(174)/0 matched multiple native boundaries [NativeCallableBoundaryId(0), NativeCallableBoundaryId(2)] for published transport boundary BoundaryId(15)

Ground truth (probed at the failure site). FunctionId(174) is `#lambda:68` -- the reduce/3 bridge wrapper `fn (entry, inner_acc) -> {:cont, reducer.(entry, inner_acc)}` (enum.fz:14). Its boundary BoundaryId(15) carries TWO resolutions that differ in EXACTLY ONE non-dispatched input -- the accumulator, `any` vs `[]` -- and are byte-identical in every codegen field: arg_reprs [ValueRef, ValueRef], return_reprs [RawAtom, ValueRef], return_shape ShapeId(39), return_ty {:cont, [a0]}. The split is pervasive: every reducer boundary (15/16/17/22) is nres=2 with the same `[]` vs `any` pair. This is the `[]`->`any` accumulator over-specialization: one closure value gets two activations because the indirect-call activation keying specializes the wrapper per precise accumulator type at each `reducer.(current, acc)` callsite, instead of once at the boundary's already-joined surface (acc erased to ValueRef).

Mechanism downstream: derive_callable_entries (artifact.rs:1841) emits one CallableEntry per resolution -> multiple NativeCallableBoundary share one (boundary, function, capture_count) -> native_boundary_for_transport_boundary (native.rs:2967) cannot pick one and errors.

Northstar (correct by construction): one published boundary => one native boundary. Fix the earliest wrong fact upstream -- collapse the reducer's resolutions to the boundary's joined surface (the `[]`/`any` accumulator over-specialization, same family as the convergence work in f98.5) so boundary_facts.resolutions is a singleton. Pin a failing transport-contract test for one-resolution-per-boundary FIRST.

Decisions flow downhill: do NOT teach native to arbitrate among boundaries. Once the upstream invariant holds, the entire native disambiguation layer is dead code and is DELETED, not patched: native_boundary_for_transport_boundary's multi-match arm, settled_callable_boundary's multi-error machinery, and select_inhabited_callable_boundary's ambiguity Result collapse to total lookups; and (folding fz-x2n) deterministic_callable_boundary_fallback and first_class_publication_boundary's fallback are removed. Net non-test shrink ~100 LoC. Blocks fz_f98_range_map_converges (bfh.4) and the to_list/run paths of fz_f98_range_reduce2.

comments.text:
Execution finding (HEAD, evidence-grounded) — the boundary fragmentation is a SYMPTOM of bridge-reducer activation over-specialization, and suppressing it only relocates the failure. Do NOT land a transport/artifact dedup patch; the holistic fix is boxed-callable activation coherence (f98.5 family).

Probed the failing `Enum.to_list` reducer (FunctionId 174 = #lambda:68, the reduce/3 wrapper `fn (entry, inner_acc) -> {:cont, reducer.(entry, inner_acc)}`):
- Each published boundary carries multiple resolutions that differ ONLY in non-dispatch input types the boundary erases to one ValueRef lane: the accumulator seen as `[]` then `any` (a subsumption pair), and the shared bridge reached over a Range (`int | float`) and a Map (`{any, any}`) entry (an incomparable pair). All share arg_reprs [ValueRef, ValueRef] and return_reprs [RawAtom, ValueRef].
- Root: convergence_collapse runs only for RECURSIVE functions (world.rs:2926); the wrapper is non-recursive, so its activations never merge. And convergence_class does NOT merge `[]`/`any` or `{any,any}`/`int|float` (distinct classes) — they coincide ONLY at the boxed codegen repr (ValueRef). Activations are type-keyed; boundaries are repr-keyed; there is no type that names "the boxed surface", which is why a simple convergence toggle does not fix it.

Tried two symptom patches; both clear the boundary error and then UNMASK pre-existing native ABI assertions that were gated behind it (confirmed pre-existing: clean HEAD hits the boundary error first):
- transport-level subsumption dedup of boundary resolutions -> terminator.rs:1142 (native tail-call lane disagreement: caller_sid 208 -> callee_sid 31, 5 args vs 6 params) and ripples ABI facts.
- artifact-level dedup of codegen-identical CallableEntries (keyed on is_empty(return_ty), since the two intern distinct return Tys that print alike) -> terminator.rs:1142 for the Range case; interp callable-entry ambiguity ("backend callable 174 ... ambiguous across entries [64,66]") and driver.rs:940 for the combined Range+Map case.

These assertions (boundary count, tail-call lane agreement, closure-target surface divergence at driver.rs:940/971, interp entry ambiguity) all detect different facets of ONE incoherence: the boxed bridge reducer is compiled as several bodies with mutually-incoherent ABIs where the runtime expects one body per (function, capture_count) dispatched through a shared identity entry. The correct-by-construction fix makes the boxed callable resolve to ONE coherent activation/body; then every assertion is satisfied because there is nothing to disambiguate. That is the boxed-callable activation-coherence design (f98.5 family), not a downstream dedup.

Recommendation: sequence f98.6 as part of / after the f98.5 activation-coherence work; the standalone transport/artifact fix is dead-ended. fz_f98_range_map_converges defers restored; tree clean.

INVESTIGATION (ground truth, repro Enum.to_list(1..3) interp on HEAD c9baed811):

PROXIMATE: native.rs native_boundary_for_transport_boundary keyed (boundary, function, capture_count) finds TWO native callable boundaries for one published BoundaryId(16), FunctionId(174)/0 (the to_list reducer lambda fn (entry, acc) -> [entry | acc]). select_inhabited_callable_boundary errors because BOTH are inhabited (the design expects at most one live).

DATA (the two MULTIMATCH boundaries):
  id 0: target_fn=FnId(55) identity_fn=FnId(71) target_input=[Ty274,Ty0,Ty0]  return_ty=Ty293 return_shape=ShapeId(39) arg_reprs=[ValueRef,ValueRef] return_lanes=[34,4]
  id 2: target_fn=FnId(56) identity_fn=FnId(71) target_input=[Ty274,Ty0,Ty37] return_ty=Ty301 return_shape=ShapeId(39) arg_reprs=[ValueRef,ValueRef] return_lanes=[34,4]
They are PHYSICALLY IDENTICAL (same arg_reprs, return_shape, return_lanes, capture_reprs=[], shared identity_fn=71); they differ ONLY in Ty-level identity (acc Ty0 vs Ty37; return Ty293 vs Ty301) and in target_fn (two separate native bodies for one source closure -> OVER-MONOMORPHIZATION). identity_fn is keyed (function, capture_count) so it is shared across all activations = the boxed closure's dispatch identity.

ROOT per the system's OWN design (native.rs settled_callable_boundary doc, ~2918): 'a value that reaches here carries a single boundary by construction... more than one boundary here means policy did not preselect, which is a TRANSPORT/ABI FACT GAP, not a choice for native.' So native is correctly refusing; the fix is UPSTREAM in TRANSPORT boundary publication. derive_callable_entries (artifact.rs:1841) emits one CallableEntry per boundary resolution; an over-monomorphized closure publishes one boundary with multiple same-function resolutions -> multiple physically-identical native entries.

FIX SHAPE (transport, fresh budget; same family as f98.3 callable-boundary identity, [[feedback_shapeid_is_pure_layout]]): a published callable boundary's NATIVE identity is its physical ABI + dispatch identity_fn, NOT the Ty-level activation. Over-monomorphized resolutions that share (identity_fn, capture_reprs, arg_reprs, return_shape, return_lanes) are ONE native callable boundary and must collapse to one entry; the per-activation target_fn is only a direct-call fast-path hint and a polymorphic boxed value (multiple live targets) carries NO single direct hint -- it dispatches via the stored identity_fn pointer. OPEN QUESTION to resolve first: confirm the boxed closure value constructed at the source stores the identity_fn(71) dispatch pointer (so dropping the direct hint routes correctly) vs a single target_fn. Then either dedup in derive_callable_entries by native-ABI+identity_fn, or have transport publish one boundary whose resolution set native maps to one native id. NOT yet implemented -- deep transport fix, checkpointed to avoid session-tail sprawl.

RESOLUTION OF SCOPE (do NOT fix at native/transport dedup): attempted the within-boundary dedup in derive_callable_entries (artifact.rs) -- it cleared the per-boundary native multi-match but the failure MOVED to the next resolver: src/ir_interp/backend.rs resolve_backend_callable_executable -> 'backend callable 174 with 0 capture(s) and 2 arg(s) is ambiguous across callable entries [55,57,59]'. Same over-monomorphization, second layer. A per-layer dedup is whack-a-mole.

CONFIRMED ROOT: the to_list reducer closure (one source lambda, one runtime identity_fn per (function,capture_count)) over-monomorphizes into N analysis activations whose accumulator types OVERLAP at runtime (acc grows [] -> [int] -> ...), so EVERY callable-resolution layer that keys by (function, capture_count, arg types) cannot tie-break them. Native boundary table AND interp backend resolver both choke; both read program.callable_entries.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS fz-f98.5 and f98.5's own trace already nailed it: 'recursive activation keys were splitting on exact tuple/list/callable evidence' (fixed via Types::convergence_class), with the remaining issue being 'transport boundary/source resolution for a first-class reducer input', and an EXPLICIT guardrail: 'Artifact/native fixes that reconstruct target identity from local shape are the wrong direction... Do not make native/codegen choose among callable boundaries.' My reverted dedup was exactly that forbidden native-layer choice.

CONCLUSION: f98.6 is a downstream symptom of the f98.5 upstream convergence / callable-flow boundary-source-resolution work, NOT an independent native/transport fix. Blocking f98.6 on f98.5; once f98.5 lands the upstream fix (accumulator activation convergence + source-to-boundary resolution for the initial reducer input), re-verify the to_list Range/Map and reduce/2 run/build symptoms here. No code change landed for f98.6 (partial native dedup reverted; tree clean at the f98.3 commit).

title: shared reduce bridge: one published callable boundary fragments into multiple native boundaries
